body.statement: Under \(\text{ass:iid-window-sampling}\), \(\inf_p\Pr_p\{p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(\widehat p)\}\ge1-\alpha\). On this single event, for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), the population envelope of \(q_j\) is contained in \(I_j^{\alpha}\), and for every distinct \(j,k\in\mathcal J\), the full same-SCM identified set of \(q_j-q_k\) is contained in \(I_{jk}^{\Delta,\alpha}\), simultaneously. Exact optimization over the closed confidence fiber remains valid at zero empirical cells. Declaring \(j\) and \(k\) tied exactly when \(0\in I_{jk}^{\Delta,\alpha}\) never asserts a strict ordering when zero is compatible with the covered observed law.
body.justification: One multinomial event provides finite-sample protection for the whole vector of nonsmooth refinement-union endpoints and decisions based on their contrasts.
body.gap: MalloyTripathyNowak2020 constructs optimal multinomial regions and DuarteEtAl2024 propagates uncertainty through one fixed-model program; EasyRCA2023 compares point direct effects without joint partial-identification or a zero-feasibility tie rule.
body.consumer: EasyRCA-style root-cause ranking can retain statistically indistinguishable candidates instead of forcing an unsupported ordering under lag and graph uncertainty.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(K=2^N\) be the number of multinomial cells.  For a fixed cell \(w\), write its \(n\) sample indicators as \(R_1,\ldots,R_n\), with \(\mathbb E R_i=p(w)\).  For completeness, set
\[
g(t)=\log\mathbb E\exp\{t(R_i-p(w))\}.
\]
Exponential tilting of a Bernoulli variable gives \(g(0)=g'(0)=0\) and
\[
g''(t)=r_t(1-r_t)\le\frac14
\]
for some tilted success probability \(r_t\in[0,1]\).  Twice integrating this inequality yields \(g(t)\le t^2/8\).  Markov's inequality and independence therefore give, for \(t>0\),
\[
\Pr_p\{\widehat p(w)-p(w)\ge\varepsilon\}
\le\exp\{-tn\varepsilon+nt^2/8\}.
\]
Minimization at \(t=4\varepsilon\) gives \(\exp(-2n\varepsilon^2)\); applying the same argument to \(-R_i\) gives
\[
\Pr_p\{|\widehat p(w)-p(w)|>\varepsilon\}
\le2\exp(-2n\varepsilon^2).
\tag{24}
\]
If the defining dyadic set for \(\varepsilon_{n,\alpha}\) is nonempty, a union bound over the \(K=2^N\) cells and (24) gives
\[
\Pr_p\{p\notin\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(\widehat p)\}
\le2^{N+1}\exp(-2n\varepsilon_{n,\alpha}^2)\le\alpha.
\tag{25}
\]
If that set is empty, \(\varepsilon_{n,\alpha}=1\), while any two probability coordinates differ by at most one; hence \(p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(\widehat p)\) surely.  This also proves (25), and the bound is uniform in \(p\).

On the event in (25), fix \(j\in\mathcal J\) and any \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\).  The choice \(p'=p\) is feasible in the corrected joint optimization defining \(I_j^\alpha\), so directly from \(\text{def:confidence-endpoints}\),
\[
\inf I_j^\alpha\le q_j(\mathcal M)\le\sup I_j^\alpha.
\]
Taking all compatible \((G,\mathcal M)\) proves containment of the whole population envelope.  The same single event works for every \(j\), so no additional union bound over \(\mathcal J\) is required.

For distinct \(j,k\), use the same \(p'=p\) and the same model \(\mathcal M\) for both queries in \(\text{def:contrast-confidence-interval}\).  It follows that every attainable same-SCM difference satisfies
\[
\inf I_{jk}^{\Delta,\alpha}
\le q_j(\mathcal M)-q_k(\mathcal M)
\le\sup I_{jk}^{\Delta,\alpha}.
\]
Again this holds for all pairs on the one event (25).

The confidence region is the intersection of a simplex with finitely many rational closed half-spaces, hence is compact even when some \(\widehat p(w)=0\).  Adding \(p'\) as a simplex variable and the rational box inequalities to each raw branch leaves a closed compact polynomial feasible set.  The argument of \(\text{thm:exact-algebraic-certification}\) therefore exactly decides emptiness or attains its extrema without dividing by an empirical cell.  Finally, whenever zero is compatible with some covered observed law and same-SCM contrast, the preceding containment puts \(0\) in \(I_{jk}^{\Delta,\alpha}\), so the stated rule declares a tie and does not assert a strict ordering.  The reverse implication need not hold because the outer interval may bridge disconnected attainable components; the rule is valid and possibly conservative.
